subject: Judge C: eager event-triggered dispatch on node-add (replace the standing drain queue)
description:
Make judgment EAGER, not a standing backlog. When a node is added/wired, a judge subagent is dispatched IMMEDIATELY to adjudicate that node's candidate edges (via task A's neighborhood-aware judge over task B's whole-graph candidates). Part of the eager-judgment-lifecycle redesign.

DESIGN:
1. On node-add (task created/wired, note created), trigger judgment for that node's unjudged candidate edges — event-driven, not the periodic drain.
2. CONCURRENCY: one dispatch per node's full edge-set (not per-edge); a small concurrency cap so a burst of node creation (e.g. a planner minting 10 tasks) doesn't fork-bomb judges. Queue excess and drain as slots free.
3. The daemon is dumb — it can't run subagents. So the trigger is the orchestration layer (heartbeat/hook reacting to new-node events, or the dispatcher). Absorbs the existing followup/judge-event-triggered work.
4. The standing 635-item drain stops being the DEFAULT path; it survives only as the timeout FALLBACK (see task D).

TEST: creating a node triggers a judge dispatch within one cycle (not waiting for a periodic drain); a burst of N nodes respects the concurrency cap; the per-node dispatch judges the whole edge-set in one shot.

GUARDRAIL: this is orchestration, not a daemon-internal loop — keep the daemon dumb (it serves candidates; the layer dispatches). Blocked by A + B (eager judgment should be the neighborhood-aware, whole-graph kind).
